title: Livin' the Dream, Pt 1, with Michael Imperioli

sentences.en: I'm Jenna Fisher.
And I'm Angela Kinsey.
We were on The Office together.
sentences.zh: 我们曾一起出演《办公室》。

sentences.en: And we're best friends.
And now we're doing the Ultimate Office Rewatch podcast just for you.
sentences.zh: 现在，我们专为你制作了这档《办公室》终极重温播客。

sentences.en: Each week, we will break down an episode of The Office and give exclusive behind-the-scenes stories that only two people who were there can tell you.
sentences.zh: 每周，我们都会剖析一集《办公室》，并分享只有身临其境的我们才能告诉你的独家幕后故事。

sentences.en: We're The Office ladies.
Oh, hi there.
Should we tell everyone how we walked in today?
sentences.zh: 我们要告诉大家我们今天是怎么走进来的吗？

sentences.en: It was ridiculous.
It's that thing.
I think when you're friends with someone, you start to, like, dress alike.
sentences.zh: 我觉得当你和某人成为朋友时，你们开始，比如，穿得像对方。

sentences.en: Because we both showed up with our hair in braids.
sentences.zh: 因为我们俩今天都扎着辫子来了。

sentences.en: Carrying giant boxes.
And then we realized they're the same exact box of iteMs.
sentences.zh: 然后我们发现那是完全一模一样的物品盒。

sentences.en: Which we'll get to later.
Yes.
But you said we should title this episode Braids and Boxes.
sentences.zh: 但你说我们应该把这集标题定为“辫子与盒子”。

sentences.en: Braids and Boxes.
Here we go.
The actual title of the episode that we're breaking down today is Live in the Dream Part 1.
sentences.zh: 我们今天剖析的这一集，实际标题是《活在梦中（上）》。

sentences.en: It is Season 9, Episode 22, written by Nikki Schwartz-Wright and directed by Jeffrey Blitz.
sentences.zh: 这是第九季第22集，由尼基·施瓦茨-赖特编剧，杰弗里·布里茨执导。

sentences.en: Would you like a summary?
So much.
All right.
In this episode, Jim is taking time off from athlete to focus on his marriage.
sentences.zh: 在这一集中，吉姆从Athlead公司请假，专注于他的婚姻。

sentences.en: Wow.
Big deal, finally.
Andy quits Dunder Mifflin to pursue his dreaMs.
sentences.zh: 安迪从邓德·米夫林辞职去追求他的梦想。

sentences.en: He's going to be something.
He might host a food show.
sentences.zh: 他可能会主持美食节目。

sentences.en: He might dance.
He might act.
There's so many options for Andy.
Anything goes.
Anything could happen.
Angela is mourning the confiscation of her cats.
sentences.zh: 安吉拉正在为她的猫被没收而哀悼。

sentences.en: All her cats get taken away in this episode.
sentences.zh: 在这一集中，她所有的猫都被带走了。

sentences.en: To Saksworth.
I know.
I remember that.
That made me laugh.
I know.
And finally, Dwight is going to receive his black belt.
sentences.zh: 最后，德怀特即将获得他的黑带。

sentences.en: Finally.
In the place he loves moSt.
Yes.
All right.
To kick things off, we got a fan question from Emma L.
sentences.zh: 首先，我们收到了一位粉丝艾玛·L的提问。

sentences.en: in Waterloo, Ontario, Canada, who said,
sentences.zh: 她来自加拿大安大略省滑铁卢，她说：

sentences.en: I want to know everything about what it was like to work with Michael Imperioli as Sensei Billy.
sentences.zh: 我想了解关于迈克尔·因佩里奥利饰演比利师傅的所有幕后故事。

sentences.en: I think his storyline and chemistry with Rainn Wilson is pure genius.
sentences.zh: 我觉得他的剧情线以及与雷恩·威尔森之间的化学反应简直是天才之作。

sentences.en: How did he come to be cast in this role?
sentences.zh: 他是怎么得到这个角色的呢？

sentences.en: Well, Emma, we are very excited to let you know that we got to interview Michael Imperioli.
sentences.zh: 艾玛，我们很高兴地告诉你，我们采访到了迈克尔·因佩里奥利。

sentences.en: We did.
All about his time on the show.
sentences.zh: 聊了他参与这部剧的全部经历。

sentences.en: And his interview is our Fast Facts 1, 2, and 3 today.
sentences.zh: 他的采访内容就是我们今天“快速事实”1、2、3期的主题。

sentences.en: So here you go.
We're so thrilled to have you.
Yeah.
Thank you.
I'm glad to be here.
It was so crazy when I was watching this episode.
sentences.zh: 我看这一集的时候觉得太不可思议了。

sentences.en: And then all of a sudden, you popped up on my screen.
sentences.zh: 突然之间，你就出现在了我的屏幕上。

sentences.en: And it was just the week before I ran into you on the street in New York.
sentences.zh: 那就在我于纽约街头偶遇你的一周之后。

sentences.en: It was right after that.
Yeah.
It was pretty wild.
It was such crazy timing.
So thanks for being with us today.
sentences.zh: 所以谢谢你今天能来参加我们的节目。

sentences.en: We'll just hop right in.
So we always ask our guests, how did you get your job on The Office?
sentences.zh: 我们总是问嘉宾，你是怎么得到《办公室》里的角色的？

sentences.en: Rainn told me that they Googled actors who were black belts.
sentences.zh: 雷恩告诉我，他们当时在谷歌上搜索拥有黑带段位的演员。

sentences.en: And your name came up?
sentences.zh: 然后就搜到了你的名字？

sentences.en: And my name was on a liSt.
So I don't know how many other actors they went through before they got to me who had black.
sentences.zh: 所以我不知道在联系到我之前，他们还找过多少其他拥有黑带的演员。

sentences.en: Maybe Chuck Norris and I don't know who else.
sentences.zh: 也许是查克·诺里斯之类的，我也不知道还有谁。

sentences.en: And that was really it.
And then I got the script and I thought it was really funny.
sentences.zh: 后来我拿到了剧本，觉得非常有趣。

sentences.en: And I mean, the show's great and really funny.
sentences.zh: 我是说，这部剧本身就很棒，而且特别好笑。

sentences.en: And that was it.
That was how I got it.
sentences.zh: 我就是这么得到这个角色的。

sentences.en: Had you watched the show before?
Yeah, like everybody on the planet pretty much.
sentences.zh: 看过，几乎地球上每个人都看过吧。

sentences.en: Yeah, I thought it was really funny.
sentences.zh: 是的，我觉得它真的很有趣。

sentences.en: And it was really a fun sequence, you know, a fun part of the episode.
sentences.zh: 那真是一段有趣的戏份，你知道，是那一集中很有意思的部分。

sentences.en: It's just so ridiculous.
It was really fun to watch it again because I hadn't seen it in quite a long time.
sentences.zh: 重温这一集真的很有趣，因为我已经很久没看了。

sentences.en: And I was like, it's even funnier than it was when I first saw it.
sentences.zh: 我当时想，它比我第一次看的时候还要好笑。

sentences.en: And when I did it, it stands up pretty well to be ridiculous and funny.
sentences.zh: 而且当我回看自己演的部分时，发现它依然非常荒谬好笑，经得起推敲。

sentences.en: It really does.
I loved Sensei Billy, like how calm he was.
sentences.zh: 我超爱比利师傅，喜欢他那种冷静的样子。

sentences.en: And just matter of fact, when Dwight's doing all this crazy crap.
sentences.zh: 当德怀特在那儿做各种疯狂举动时，他却表现得那么一本正经。

sentences.en: Well, listen, there are three scenes that you're in.
sentences.zh: 听着，你在剧中总共有三场戏。

sentences.en: You know, one of them is the very first montage where Dwight's trying to kick the board, which is hilarious.
sentences.zh: 其中一场是最初的蒙太奇片段，德怀特试图踢碎木板，那段真是太搞笑了。

sentences.en: Did you give Rain any tips or did he just like go for it?
sentences.zh: 你有给雷恩什么建议吗，还是他直接就上手了？

sentences.en: No, he just went for it.
You know, I've done Korean martial arts, mostly taekwondo for like 22 years.
sentences.zh: 你知道，我练过韩国武术，主要是跆拳道，练了大概22年。

sentences.en: And sometimes you do break boards, you know, that's part of it.
sentences.zh: 有时候确实需要踢碎木板，那是练习的一部分。

sentences.en: Like usually on a test, when you're going up a level or something, you do that as a, you know, you're testing your kind of accuracy and speed and things like that.
sentences.zh: 通常在晋级考试之类的场合，你会通过这种方式来测试自己的精准度、速度以及诸如此类的能力。

sentences.en: And I've never gotten kicked in the balls doing that, but I've held boards for other people, testing, especially for kids.
sentences.zh: 我做那个动作时从来没被踢到过裆部，但我帮别人拿过木板，做测试的时候，尤其是给小孩子拿。

sentences.en: Kids aren't as accurate as adults sometimes.
sentences.zh: 小孩子有时候没那么准。

sentences.en: And they'll kick your hands and, you know, holding boards for people.
sentences.zh: 他们会踢到你的手，你知道的，帮人拿木板就是这样。

sentences.en: I've gotten my hands pretty banged up.
So that's kind of accurate.
That really happens.
But he just went for it.
You know, I don't remember if he told me that he trained or not.
sentences.zh: 你知道，我不记得他有没有跟我说他练过。

sentences.en: I'm pretty sure he had not trained.
He had not trained, yeah.
It didn't seem like he did.
But he just went for it.
And, I mean, it's just so silly and fun.
sentences.zh: 而且，我是说，这真的太傻太好玩了。

sentences.en: It's so silly.
And then the next one is the belt ceremony in the office, the place he loves the most, right?
sentences.zh: 接下来就是办公室里的腰带授予仪式，他最喜欢的地方，对吧？

sentences.en: And then you couldn't get the belt off him and he's kind of awkwardly thrusting at you.
sentences.zh: 然后你没法把腰带从他身上解下来，他还在那儿笨拙地对着你挺胯。

sentences.en: And you're so, since I'm Billy, she's like, this isn't going to work.
sentences.zh: 而你，因为我是比利，她就觉得，这可不行。

sentences.en: Okay.
He's trying his best to keep composure because that's what a martial artist does, right?
sentences.zh: 他正努力保持镇定，因为那是武术家该做的，对吧？

sentences.en: He's, you know, he doesn't let his anger get the best of him.
sentences.zh: 他，你知道，他不会让愤怒冲昏头脑。

sentences.en: But, you know, in martial arts, a lot of the movements, most of them really come from the hips, from the center of the body.
sentences.zh: 但是，你知道，在武术中，很多动作，大部分确实来自髋部，来自身体中心。

sentences.en: You know, that's really where you get your power if you're throwing a punch.
sentences.zh: 你知道，如果你要出拳，力量确实就是从那儿来的。

sentences.en: You know, if you watch like athletes like golfers or baseball players or tennis players, you can see it.
sentences.zh: 你知道，如果你观察像高尔夫球手、棒球运动员或网球运动员这样的运动员，你就能看出来。

sentences.en: Like those, yeah, those motions with the arMs.
sentences.zh: 就像那些，没错，那些手臂的动作。

sentences.en: Yeah.
I have a really good forehand.
I don't want to brag, but I have a really, well, now I'm bragging, but I have a really good forehand at tennis.
sentences.zh: 我不想吹牛，但我确实，好吧，现在我是在吹牛了，但我的网球正手真的很厉害。

sentences.en: And I'm short and people don't expect it because it's all in that twist, that torque from your hips.
sentences.zh: 我个子不高，人们对此没抱太大期望，因为关键全在于那种扭转，那种来自髋部的扭矩。

sentences.en: So a lot of the movements in martial arts come from the hips, like punches and blocks and kicks even, right?
sentences.zh: 所以武术中的很多动作都来自髋部，比如出拳、格挡，甚至踢腿，对吧？

sentences.en: So I think that's what he was, he was figuring, I have to use my hips here.
sentences.zh: 所以我认为他当时就是这么想的，我得在这儿用上我的髋部。

sentences.en: You know, even getting the belt, like everything we do comes from the hips and it wasn't necessary.
sentences.zh: 你知道，甚至连拿腰带也是，我们做的每件事都来自髋部，虽然没必要。

sentences.en: I love that.
That's my theory, at leaSt.
Do you remember like breaking it all in that scene?
sentences.zh: 你还记得那场戏里大家都笑场了吗？

sentences.en: Because I remember watching it and I, I think there's no shots of me in this sequence because they had to avoid me because I couldn't keep it together.
sentences.zh: 因为我记得看那段的时候，我想这段戏里没有我的镜头，因为他们得避开我，我当时根本憋不住笑。

sentences.en: No, I lost it a few times.
It was just so, you know, he's just so committed, you know.
sentences.zh: 实在是太，你知道，他当时太投入了，你知道的。

sentences.en: Fans wrote in and pointed out every time someone broke and it's, we're all, they clocked everybody.
sentences.zh: 粉丝们写信指出每次有人笑场的情况，我们所有人都被他们盯上了。

sentences.en: Except you.
My memory, Michael, is that you were very good at keeping it together.
sentences.zh: 迈克尔，我的记忆是，你非常擅长憋笑。

sentences.en: Are you an actor that breaks a lot?
sentences.zh: 你是个容易笑场的演员吗？

sentences.en: Because I was so impressed.
sentences.zh: 因为我当时印象非常深刻。

sentences.en: If it's really funny.
Yeah.
Sometimes.
You know, on The Sopranos, the time everybody broke was when it was the mother, Livia's post-funeral gathering at The Soprano House.
sentences.zh: 你知道，在《黑道家族》里，大家全都笑场的那次，是在利维亚的葬礼后，在黑道家族的房子里聚会的时候。

sentences.en: And everybody's there, the whole family and all the gangsters and all the friends of the family.
sentences.zh: 每个人都在那儿，整个家族，所有的黑帮成员，还有所有家族的朋友。

sentences.en: They're talking about this woman that everybody hated, really, and who hated everybody, trying to find nice things to say.
sentences.zh: 他们在谈论这个大家其实都很讨厌的女人，而她也讨厌所有人，大家都在努力找些好话来说。

sentences.en: And then they play her favorite song, which was this really schmaltzy love song from Carousel sung in this very high-pitched voice.
sentences.zh: 然后他们放了她最喜欢的歌，那是《旋转木马》里的一首非常煽情的爱情歌曲，用那种很尖的嗓音唱出来的。

sentences.en: And when they put that song on, everybody just lost it.
sentences.zh: 当他们放那首歌的时候，所有人都彻底破功了。

sentences.en: And they tried to do it again.
And every time that song came on, everybody just lost it.
sentences.zh: 每次那首歌一响，大家就彻底失控了。

sentences.en: And then they realized, well, we can't play the song.
sentences.zh: 后来他们意识到，好吧，我们不能放这首歌。

sentences.en: So let's just pretend we're listening to it.
sentences.zh: 所以我们假装在听就好了。

sentences.en: And that still didn't work.
To the point where the director started yelling at people.
sentences.zh: 以至于导演开始对大家大吼大叫。

sentences.en: It was totally out of character for him because he had directed a lot of our episodes.
sentences.zh: 这完全不像他平时的作风，因为他执导过我们很多集。

sentences.en: And he was a sweetheart.
But he just couldn't do the scene because we were just, it just became this thing that was just too ridiculous.
sentences.zh: 但他就是拍不了那场戏，因为我们当时的状态实在太荒唐了。

sentences.en: It's hard to come back from that, too.
sentences.zh: 那种状态也很难恢复过来。

sentences.en: When you're gone, you know, when you're in that kind of laughter fit.
sentences.zh: 当你陷入那种狂笑不止的状态时，你知道的。

sentences.en: No, you can't.
It's so hard to come back.
Yeah, you have to stop.
You have to, you need some time.
sentences.zh: 你必须得停，你需要一点时间。

sentences.en: You know, the Brits call that corpsing.
sentences.zh: 你知道吗，英国人把这叫做“尸体化”。

sentences.en: You know that, right?
I did not know that.
That's what they call it.
Yeah, yeah, yeah, yeah.
Because you're just dead.
sentences.zh: 因为你就像死了一样（僵住了）。

sentences.en: They call it corpsing when you just can't stop laughing, which is a weird expression, right?
sentences.zh: 他们把这种无法停止大笑的状态称为“尸体化”，这说法挺奇怪的，对吧？

sentences.en: It is.
But I love it.
That happened to Jenna and I when I had to tell her that Dwight put sprinkles in my freezer.
sentences.zh: 我和珍娜拍那场戏时就发生了这种情况，当时我得告诉她德怀特把“洒洒”放进了我的冷冻柜里。

sentences.en: And I had to ask her if Roy had ever mercy killed one of her pets.
sentences.zh: 我还得问她罗伊有没有对她的宠物实施过安乐死。

sentences.en: We couldn't.
Every time.
They had to go to lunch.
sentences.zh: 他们只好让我们去吃午饭。

sentences.en: I said, like, the cat had clawed the peas, like, the bag of peas because the cat was trying to get out of the freezer.
sentences.zh: 我说那只猫抓破了豌豆袋，因为猫想从冷冻柜里逃出来。

sentences.en: They broke us for lunch.
sentences.zh: 他们不得不让我们中场休息去吃午饭。

sentences.en: They were like, you're gone.
sentences.zh: 他们说，你们彻底没救了。

sentences.en: You're corpsing.
You need time.
Forget it.
Yeah, because at that point, everything's going to be funny no matter how, you know, how you approach it.
sentences.zh: 是啊，因为到了那个地步，无论你怎么处理，一切都会变得很好笑。

sentences.en: And it's infectious and it's uncontrollable.
sentences.zh: 而且这种情绪会传染，根本控制不住。

sentences.en: It's an interesting phenomenon.
And you can't really explain it to anyone unless you're really, because you're acting, you're not supposed to laugh, right?
sentences.zh: 你很难向别人解释，除非你亲身经历，因为你在演戏，你不应该笑，对吧？

sentences.en: Which makes it worse, I think.
sentences.zh: 我觉得这反而让情况更糟了。

sentences.en: Makes it worse, yeah.
It's like, don't think of the word elephant or something.
sentences.zh: 就像那种“别去想大象”之类的心理暗示。

sentences.en: It's kind of like that.
Well, speaking of laughing, after the belt thrusting, we get to Dwight's demonstration.
sentences.zh: 说到笑，在腰带猛冲动作之后，就到了德怀特的演示环节。

sentences.en: Yeah.
Which is so incredible.
I have to ask, with all of your experience, is anything he's doing in this scene accurate in any way?
sentences.zh: 我得问问，以你的经验，他在那场戏里做的动作有任何准确的地方吗？

sentences.en: Is he doing any actual moves here?
sentences.zh: 他做的那些动作有实际意义吗？

sentences.en: You know, some of the basic techniques he's executing, but he doesn't really know how to do them properly.
sentences.zh: 你知道，他用了一些基本技巧，但他其实并不知道怎么正确地做出来。

sentences.en: Okay.
Is Sensei Billy giving him a black belt, like, sort of patronizingly?
sentences.zh: 比利老师给他黑带，是不是有点居高临下的意思？

sentences.en: Has he earned his black belt, in your opinion?
sentences.zh: 在你看来，他拿到黑带是实至名归吗？

sentences.en: I think he's earned it.
sentences.zh: 我觉得他是实至名归的。

sentences.en: Well, he said he's one of the most tenacious people he's ever seen.
sentences.zh: 嗯，他说过这是他见过最坚韧的人之一。

sentences.en: So, I think that tenaciousness.
sentences.zh: 所以，我觉得那种坚韧劲儿。

sentences.en: You know, a black belt in martial arts, you have to remember, is you're not competing or comparing your level of skill and your development to anyone else.
sentences.zh: 你要知道，武术里的黑带，你得记住，它不是让你去和别人竞争，也不是让你拿自己的技术水平和成长进度去跟别人比。

sentences.en: It's about your progression.
sentences.zh: 它关乎的是你自己的进步。

sentences.en: So, you can have a black belt, two black belts that have trained the same amount of time, and one's a super great athlete, and one's not.
sentences.zh: 所以，你可以有两个都练了同样长时间的黑带选手，其中一个运动天赋超群，另一个则不然。

sentences.en: And they're going to be very different martial artists, you know, because natural athleticism and stuff, you know, I mean, I'm 58.
sentences.zh: 他们会成为非常不同的武术家，因为天生的运动能力之类的因素，你知道，毕竟我都58岁了。

sentences.en: I still train.
But, you know, you see some of these kids at 25 doing stuff that's just incredible that I'm not going to do.
sentences.zh: 但是，你会看到一些25岁的年轻人做出的动作简直不可思议，我是做不到了。

sentences.en: I mean, I have basic techniques that I've worked on for many years that I'm comfortable with.
